_doc: Canonical lifecycles of IVG (playbook 3.3a step 3), semantics lane, pin 3eaa79cf. One name and one meaning per state and per command. A facet is a property orthogonal to the lifecycle state (approval and block in the playbook; here: governed, marked, read-only, layout, ...); an object maps each of its ontology states to one canonical state, optionally with facets, and each of its ontology commands to one canonical command of its lifecycle. Object declarations: semantics/objects.json. State and command ids are unique in meaning across lifecycles (the same id recurs only where the meaning is the same: absent = no instance exists; read = answer or report without changing anything; restore = put archived content back into the live stores, seen from the item (LC-1) or from the copy (LC-8); erase = remove every item of a scope, seen from the item (LC-1) or the scope (LC-6)). Renamed after the mapping lane's report: LC-3 current -> in-force, LC-3 use -> consult, LC-2 failed -> build-failed, LC-7 failed -> errored; after the checker's vocabulary rule: LC-4 commit -> append (LC-7 commit ends a transaction). Ids that recur with one meaning seen from two levels: absent, read, restore, erase, live (SYS-D13: some store holds the content, of an item or of a scope), upgrade (bring to the current release's layout or setup), redact (turn history into tombstones, of a record or of a scope).

lifecycles.name: Content item
lifecycles.meaning: A piece of graph content a caller writes: a node, edge, label, property, qualifier, temporal event, vector, text document or reifier, in one graph.

states.meaning: no store holds the item in its graph
some primary store holds the item in its graph (SYS-D13)

commands.meaning: make the item live (also store, insert, merge-create, bulk create)
change a live item's value (set, reweight, replace, merge-match)
make one item absent by its id
make every item of a graph or id prefix absent (module 12)
answer from the item without changing it
bring the item back from an archive (module 18)

facets: marked (implied by a temporal write, ADR-0009)
shared id (the same id is live in another graph)
orphan (outlived the item it depends on)
rolled back (an open writer's write was undone)

lifecycles.name: Derived entry
lifecycles.meaning: A store or entry computed from other stores: an index, a cache entry, a compiled plan, a statement map, an aggregate.

states.meaning: not built
a build or upgrade is in progress
equals its derivation from the committed source (stamp equals token)
known not to equal its derivation; readers must not trust it
a build failed; readers fall back to the source

commands.meaning: compute from the source and stamp it
a source write that updates the entry in its transaction or marks it stale
answer from the entry after checking its signal
recompute from the source, replacing the entry
remove the entry
move the entry to a newer layout

facets: degraded (written without its lock, with a mark)

lifecycles.name: Setting or install
lifecycles.meaning: A configuration of a namespace, a graph, a process or a deployment: the install, the class set, the ledger state, a graph's mode, a route registration, an optional dependency.

states.meaning: not set up or not present
set up and in force
present from an earlier release or setup; needs an upgrade or forced setup
a setup started and did not finish
present but unusable or in conflict (another schema, another app, a bad value)
set up and switched off

commands.meaning: create or bring in force (deploy, setup, register, create web app, map)
change one value of a setting in force (turn on/off, set strict, set mode)
move from outdated to in force (forced setup, migration, adopt)
take the setting or install away (legacy removal, unmap, drop)
report the setting (status, info, preview, list)
run a command that depends on the setting (first use, a call under the mode)

lifecycles.name: History item
lifecycles.meaning: An item of the revision ledger: a revision, a record, a retry-key binding.

states.meaning: not yet committed (a retry key: free)
saved in a revision and never changed since (a retry key: bound)
redacted: keeps its place, holds no content (a retry key: redacted)

commands.meaning: append in a new revision
a retry answered from the binding, with no effect
turn into a tombstone
read history (history, records, diff, verify, export)

lifecycles.name: Run
lifecycles.meaning: Work that takes several steps or is done later: a queue entry, a redaction run, a sync, a build job.

states.meaning: not requested
requested and waiting for a worker
a worker is on it
interrupted, with its effects so far kept; can be resumed
finished with its result
finished without its result, reported

commands.meaning: request the work (enqueue, call, schedule)
a worker step
interrupt (process stop, a bound reached, the ledger disabled)
call again after a stop
mark done or failed
remove finished entries
report the state

lifecycles.name: Scope
lifecycles.meaning: A graph or a tenant target (a graph plus an optional id prefix) as a whole.

states.meaning: no content and no history
holds content
an erasure is open on it
no content; history still holds its records
a redaction run is open on it (marker set)
no content and its history is tombstoned

commands.meaning: a commit or direct write of content into the scope
remove the scope's content from every store
remove the scope's content from history
a read or verify of the scope

lifecycles.name: Session, request or claim
lifecycles.meaning: Something held for a while by one caller: a transaction, a reader handle, a Bolt session, an HTTP request, a connection, a lock.

states.meaning: created, not yet accepted (not logged in, not begun)
in use by its holder
ended normally; its outcome was delivered
ended by an explicit refusal before any effect
ended by an error; its effect may be unknown

commands.meaning: begin, log in, connect, take the lock
a step inside it (run, read a page, write)
end keeping its writes
end dropping its writes
end it, release what it holds

lifecycles.name: Copy
lifecycles.meaning: A copy of content kept outside the live stores: a snapshot archive, a quarantined vector.

states.meaning: no copy
the copy exists and holds content
the copy was placed back or restored and no longer holds what it released

commands.meaning: make the copy
put the copy's content back (replacing or merging, or placing a quarantined row)
report on the copy
delete the copy
